content: Choline kinase alpha (CHKA) is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the CHKA gene. The primary pathway for the biosynthesis of phosphatidylcholine occurs through the CDP-choline pathway. The protein encoded by the CHKA gene serves as the initial enzyme in this biosynthetic sequence and is thought to play a regulatory role in the process. Additionally, the encoded protein is responsible for catalyzing the phosphorylation of ethanolamine. Two transcript variants of the CHKA gene have been identified, each encoding distinct isoforms of the enzyme. In melanocytic cells, the expression of the CHKA gene may be regulated by the microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF).
